source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025), in conjunction with ISCA 2025, June 21, 2025, Tokyo, Japan, pp. 1-6.

summary: The register component (sR) enhances the Statistical Corrector (SC) by capturing correlations between recently produced register values and branch directions. Instead of tracking data-flow dependency chains between producer instructions and branches, sR globally monitors available architectural register values using 12-bit compressed digests generated upon instruction completion. Registers are partitioned across eight banks. For each bank, 3-table usefulness tables (UT) track which registers provide high correlation with branch outcomes; the most useful currently available register in each bank is selected to index 3-table prediction weight tables (WT). Positive-usefulness bank contributions are scaled by 2.5 and summed to produce sR, which directly enters the SC LSUM. To maintain freshness and prevent stale correlations, entries decay and are invalidated after 256 subsequent decoded instructions.

state.name: Register Status and Digest Table (Auxiliary Data)
state.organization: Direct-mapped table indexed by logical register ID, 65 entries (covering 65 logical registers: R0 to R64)
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit) + payload (14 bits: either 14-bit ROB tag or 12-bit register digest) + decay_ctr (8 bits)
state.indexing: Direct indexing by architectural/logical register ID (0 to 64)

state.name: Register Usefulness Weight Tables (UT)
state.organization: 8 banks (Banks 0-7), each containing 3 tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each. Bank 0 covers 9 registers (R0, R8, ..., R64); Banks 1-7 cover 8 registers each (R[b + 8*k]). Each entry stores a vector of 6-bit signed weights corresponding to the bank's registers.
state.entry_format: Bank 0 entries: 9 x 6-bit signed saturating weights (54 bits/entry). Banks 1-7 entries: 8 x 6-bit signed saturating weights (48 bits/entry). Total 65 registers x 3 tables x 8 entries x 6 bits.
state.indexing: UT0, UT1, UT2 indexed by 3-bit skewed hashes of PC: hash_ut(PC, table_id, bank_id) mod 8

state.name: Register Prediction Weight Tables (WT)
state.organization: 8 banks (Banks 0-7), each containing 3 tables: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), WT2 (128 entries). Entries are 6-bit signed saturating weights.
state.indexing: WT0, WT1, WT2 indexed by hashes combining PC and the selected 12-bit register digest: hash_wt(PC, reg_digest, table_id) modulo table size (512, 256, 128)

algorithms.name: digest_generation
algorithms.trigger: Instruction execution complete / value produced at functional unit
algorithms.notes: Digest generation compresses 64-bit values to 12 bits. In FP mode, bits [2:0] remain unused (0). In INT mode, counts saturate at 63 if matching length is 64.

algorithms.name: instruction_decode
algorithms.trigger: Instruction decode time for an instruction writing a destination register
algorithms.notes: Emulates Tomasulo register status: destination register is marked busy/invalid and points to the producing ROB entry.

algorithms.name: instruction_complete
algorithms.trigger: Instruction completion / writeback when destination value is produced
algorithms.notes: Sets valid bit and stores the 12-bit digest in payload. Initializes decay counter.

algorithms.name: digest_decay_tick
algorithms.trigger: Decode of each subsequent instruction (instruction-driven clock)
algorithms.notes: Invalidates digests after 256 instructions to prevent stale values from poisoning correlation.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.trigger: Branch fetch / prediction time (SC evaluation phase)
algorithms.notes: Bank contribution is scaled by 2.5 when selected register usefulness is positive, and suppressed (x0) otherwise or when no register in the bank is valid. sR_sum feeds directly into SC LSUM.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.trigger: Branch resolution / commit time (SC update trigger: SC misprediction or |LSUM| <= Update_Threshold)
algorithms.pseudocode:
function update_sR(branch_pc, actual_dir, sc_correct, pred_snapshot):
    for b = 0 to 7:
        valid_regs = pred_snapshot.bank_valid_regs[b]
        if valid_regs is empty:
            continue
        
        // Training rule: randomly select one available register within the bank
        reg_to_update = valid_regs[random_choice(len(valid_regs))]
        sub_idx = register_index_in_bank(reg_to_update, b)
        
        idx0 = hash_ut(branch_pc, 0, b)
        idx1 = hash_ut(branch_pc, 1, b)
        idx2 = hash_ut(branch_pc, 2, b)
        
        // Update usefulness weights in UT (increment if this bank predicted correctly, decrement if wrong)
        ut_dir = +1 if (sc_correct) else -1
        saturating_add(UT[b][0][idx0][sub_idx], ut_dir, -32, 31)
        saturating_add(UT[b][1][idx1][sub_idx], ut_dir, -32, 31)
        saturating_add(UT[b][2][idx2][sub_idx], ut_dir, -32, 31)
        
        // Update prediction weights in WT for this register's digest
        digest = reg_table[reg_to_update].payload & 0x0FFF
        h0 = hash_wt(branch_pc, digest, 0) % 512
        h1 = hash_wt(branch_pc, digest, 1) % 256
        h2 = hash_wt(branch_pc, digest, 2) % 128
        
        wt_dir = +1 if (actual_dir == TAKEN) else -1
        saturating_add(WT[b][0][h0], wt_dir, -32, 31)
        saturating_add(WT[b][1][h1], wt_dir, -32, 31)
        saturating_add(WT[b][2][h2], wt_dir, -32, 31)
algorithms.notes: Only registers available at prediction time are eligible. Randomly selecting one register per bank guarantees that each WT and UT table needs only a single write port.

algorithms.name: mispredict_recovery
algorithms.notes: Upon branch misprediction recovery, tags matching flushed instructions are invalidated. Registers whose producer finished prior to or during the flush remain valid and immediately become available to subsequent restart predictions.

host_interfaces.need: Register write destination and ROB index at decode
host_interfaces.description: Host notifies branch predictor when an instruction targeting a logical register is decoded, passing destination register ID and ROB allocation tag.
host_interfaces.fallback: In trace-based or execution-driven simulators without out-of-order decode/ROB modeling, treat register values as valid and immediately available at instruction completion, bypassing decode-time invalidation.

host_interfaces.need: Execution completion / writeback register values and register class
host_interfaces.description: Functional units provide produced 64-bit value, destination register ID, and register type (INT, FP, FLAG) upon completion.
host_interfaces.fallback: Infer register type from register ID (e.g. R0-R31 as INT, R32-R63 as FP, R64 as FLAG).

host_interfaces.need: Decoded instruction count for digest decay
host_interfaces.description: Host signals each decoded instruction or retired instruction to advance the 8-bit digest decay counter.
host_interfaces.fallback: Advance decay counter on each branch prediction call scaled by an average basic block size (e.g. +5 instructions per branch).

host_interfaces.description: Host notifies predictor of branch squash and provides the set of squashed ROB tags.
host_interfaces.fallback: Flush all in-flight invalid tags upon misprediction, retaining only previously committed register values.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: Prediction Weight Tables (WT): 8 banks x (512 + 256 + 128 entries) x 6 bits = 43,008 bits. Usefulness Weight Tables (UT): 65 registers x 3 tables x 8 entries x 6 bits = 9,360 bits. Auxiliary Data: 65 register entries x (1 valid + 14 payload + 8 decay_ctr) = 1,495 bits. Total: 43008 + 9360 + 1495 = 53863 bits (6.57 KiB).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires 8 parallel 8-way/9-way comparators (one per bank) to find the maximum usefulness value among valid registers, three hash XOR-networks for WT indexing per bank, single-write-port SRAMs, and INT/FP digest generation bitwise XOR/shift logic.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: To fit within iso-storage budgets, tagged tables in TAGE (e.g., reducing high-bank tag widths or bank entry counts) or secondary SC tables (such as sS or sT local history tables) can be trimmed.

parameters.name: num_banks
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales WT storage and UT entry grouping.

parameters.name: num_logical_registers
parameters.storage_impact: Linearly scales UT bits (144 bits per register) and Auxiliary table bits (23 bits per register).

parameters.name: decay_limit
parameters.storage_impact: None as long as decay_ctr remains 8 bits; requires ceil(log2(decay_limit)) bits per register.

parameters.name: wt_weight_width
parameters.storage_impact: Linearly scales WT storage (7168 entries * width).

parameters.name: ut_weight_width
parameters.storage_impact: Linearly scales UT storage (1560 weights * width).

parameters.name: wt_entries
parameters.storage_impact: Scales WT capacity proportionally to sum of entry counts across tables.

unit_tests.name: int_digest_generation_known_values
unit_tests.given: 64-bit integer value 0x0000000000000008 (leading zeros = 60, trailing zeros = 3, LSB6 = 8).

unit_tests.name: fp64_digest_extraction
unit_tests.given: 64-bit float with sign=1, exponent=0x401 (binary 10000000001, top 8 exponent bits = 10000000). Source bits [63:55] = 0x180.
unit_tests.expect: Extracted slice is placed at digest[11:3]: digest = 0x180 << 3 = 0xC00, digest[2:0] = 0.

unit_tests.name: bank_assignment_mapping
unit_tests.given: Logical registers R0, R1, R8, R15, R64.
unit_tests.expect: R0 maps to Bank 0, R1 to Bank 1, R8 to Bank 0, R15 to Bank 7, R64 to Bank 0. Bank 0 contains 9 registers; Banks 1-7 contain 8 registers.

unit_tests.name: digest_decay_invalidation
unit_tests.given: Register R4 completed with valid digest at cycle 0. Exactly 256 subsequent instructions are decoded without new writes to R4.
unit_tests.expect: At instruction 255, reg_table[R4].valid == 1 and decay_ctr == 255. At instruction 256, reg_table[R4].valid transitions to 0.

unit_tests.name: predict_usefulness_thresholding
unit_tests.given: Bank 1 has valid register R9 with sum of UT weights = -2, and no other valid registers. WT sum for R9 digest is +15.
unit_tests.expect: Because max usefulness <= 0, Bank 1's contribution is scaled by x0, yielding 0 contribution to sR.

unit_tests.name: predict_usefulness_scaling
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 has valid register R0 with sum of UT weights = +5. WT weights are WT0=2, WT1=3, WT2=1 (sum = +6).
unit_tests.expect: Because usefulness > 0, Bank 0's contribution is floor(6 * 2.5) = 15.

open_questions: Exact condition for multiplier selection (x0 vs x2.5): the paper shows 'x0 or x2.5' downstream of WT summation per bank. The spec assumes x2.5 applies when max_useful > 0 and a valid register exists, and x0 otherwise, but this control wire is not explicitly labelled in Figure 5(c).
Leading/trailing zero or one counter saturation: a 64-bit word can have 64 identical bits, requiring 7 bits to represent without loss. The spec assumes counts saturate at 63 (0x3F) to fit in 6 bits.

Floating-point format classification: Section 4.2 states format is classified by inspecting MSBs, but does not provide the exact bitmask logic used to distinguish FP16, FP32, and FP64 in a unified register file.
Hash functions: the specific polynomial/skewing functions for hash_ut(PC) and hash_wt(PC, reg_digest) are not detailed in the paper text; standard folded XOR hashes are assumed.

Ties in UT max selection: when multiple valid registers in a bank have identical maximum usefulness, the tie-break rule (e.g. lowest register index) is not specified; arbitrary first-match is assumed.
